column5: source
column6: target

column5: I nod. I guess he {i}does{/i} have the authority here.{w}\nAfter all, none of us know anything about this place.{w}\nIf we're following his lead, I'd better do what he says.
column6: 我点点头。看来他在这里{i}确实{/i}有权威。{w}\n毕竟，我们对这个地方一无所知。{w}\n既然要跟着他走，我最好照他说的做。

column5: Of course, I do have a few questions about this place.{w}\nIf I stop to ask him before we leave, I better do it fast.{w}\nMissing that ball could be catastrophic to our cause.
column6: 当然，关于这个地方我确实有些疑问。{w}\n如果我要在出发前停下来问他，最好快一点。{w}\n错过那场舞会对我们的事业可能是灾难性的。

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: Well, it's definitely not something Draycu came up with.\nRulers of Alarinthia have been doing it for ages, actually.\nIt's supposed to make your subjects less inclined to rebel.
column6: 嗯，这绝对不是德雷库想出来的。\n其实，阿拉林西亚的统治者们这么做已经很久了。\n据说是为了让臣民不那么容易造反。

column5: It's not really working, if Vivien exists.\nBut at the end of the day, it's still a nice party.\nAs much food and drink as you could ever want.
column6: 如果薇薇安还存在着，那这招其实不太管用。\n但说到底，那依然是个不错的派对。\n食物和美酒管够，你想要多少有多少。

column5: Don't worry, [firstname]. I won't go overboard.\nI do like to drink, but not while I'm on a mission of any sort.\nI'll be tempted of course — though I'm sure you can keep me in line.
column6: 别担心，[firstname]。我不会太过分的。\n我确实爱喝酒，但绝不会在执行任何任务的时候喝。\n当然我会受到诱惑——不过我确信你能管住我。

column5: After the feast, there's a large ball. But it all starts with a speech.\nBasically, Draycu will be bragging about his power and influence.\nIf he shows off how strong he is, he's less inclined to be challenged.
column6: 宴会之后有一场盛大的舞会。不过一切都以一场演讲开始。\n基本上，德雷库会吹嘘自己的权势和影响力。\n只要他展示出自己有多强，就没人敢轻易挑战他。

column5: Though if there {i}is{/i} a challenge, they hold a tournament the next day.\nIt rarely happens, unless it's a drunken partygoer trying to play a joke.\nEveryone wakes up, hung over, and goes about their simple lives.
column6: 不过如果{i}真的{/i}有人挑战，他们第二天会举办一场比武大会。\n这种情况很少见，除非是哪个喝醉的宾客想开个玩笑。\n大家醒来，宿醉未消，继续各自平淡的生活。

column5: Honestly, I don't know too much about him.\nI've been out of the loop on Alarinthian politics for a while.\nBut to hold the throne of this nation, you need to be fierce.
column6: 老实说，我对他了解不多。\n我已经很久没关注阿拉林西亚的政事了。\n但要想坐稳这个国家的王座，你必须够凶狠。

column5: So if you think I'm strong, then you know nothing.\nHe'll make me look like a whelp in comparison.\nAnd from what I've heard, he's pretty smart, too.
column6: 所以如果你觉得我算强，那你就是什么都不懂。\n跟他一比，我会显得像只小崽子。\n而且据我所知，他还相当聪明。

column5: Most rulers, from what I've seen, simply bathe in their own riches.\nTo hold a ball and share it with your nation? That's pretty genius.\nIt destroys any motivation to remove him from the throne.
column6: 据我所见，大多数统治者只是沉溺于自己的财富之中。\n举办一场舞会，与全国百姓共享？那真是相当高明。\n这彻底打消了人们把他赶下王座的念头。

column5: That's why Alarinthia hasn't had a tournament in a long time.\nThe people are either happy, or certain that they'd lose in combat.\nI'm betting on the latter, which makes Draycu even more intimidating.
column6: 这就是为什么阿拉林西亚很久没举办过比武大会了。\n百姓要么心满意足，要么确信自己会在战斗中落败。\n我赌是后者，这让德雷库显得更加令人畏惧。

column5: Do {i}not{/i} underestimate him, [firstname].\nIf the natives can't dethrone him, what chance do we stand?\nVivien might dream of a changed nation, but it'll stay that. Just a dream.
column6: {i}千万别{/i}小看他，[firstname]。\n如果本地人都推翻不了他，我们又能有多少胜算？\n薇薇安也许梦想着改变这个国家，但那终究只是梦想。仅此而已。

column5: The Town Square is a nice place. But it's just like Mazeo.\nA large market, with people all peddling their homemade wares.\nYou won't find anything you need, but you'll find everything you {i}want{/i}.
column6: 城镇广场是个不错的地方。但和马泽奥差不多。\n一个大集市，人们都在兜售自家做的东西。\n你找不到任何你需要的东西，但你能找到所有你{i}想要{/i}的东西。

column5: After that, I'd say to pay the coliseum a visit.\nIt's not just a venue used to battle for Alarinthia's throne.\nThey have large battles every day, and you can place bets.
column6: 之后，我建议去斗兽场看看。\n它不只是用来争夺阿拉林西亚王座的场地。\n那里每天都举行大型战斗，你还可以下注。

column5: Of course, my personal pick would be the tavern.\nAlarinthia has a lot of unique drinks, so I'll make sure to stop there.\nIf I get my fill, maybe I'll be lucky enough to forget this entire voyage.
column6: 当然，我个人的首选会是酒馆。\n阿拉林西亚有很多独特的饮品，所以我一定会去那里。\n如果能喝个痛快，也许我还能幸运地忘掉这整趟旅程。

column5: It doesn't feel any different than I thought, if that's what you mean.\nStepping foot on this soil didn't change my mind. It only solidified my hate.\nLet's do everything we can to get out of here as fast possible, [firstname]. Please.
column6: 如果你是这个意思的话，感觉跟我预想的没什么两样。\n踏上这片土地并没有改变我的想法，只是更加深了我的憎恨。\n我们尽可能快点离开这里吧，[firstname]。求你了。

column5: No. I just want to get the job done, and get back home.\nIf you think you can change my outlook on this place, you're wrong.\nI think this conversation is over, [firstname]. We have a long journey ahead.
column6: 不。我只想完成任务，然后回家。\n如果你以为能改变我对这个地方的看法，那你就错了。\n我想这场谈话到此为止了，[firstname]。我们还有很长的路要走。

column5: Is that Alarinthia? It's huge.
column6: 那就是阿拉林西亚吗？好大。

column5: No, it's not. That's just immigration.
column6: 不，不是。那只是入境关卡。

column5: Immigration?
column6: 入境关卡？

column5: Yeah. If you're an outsider, you need to register.\nThat is, of course, except during Draycu's annual ball.
column6: 对。如果你是外来者，就得登记。\n当然，德雷库一年一度的舞会期间除外。

column5: So we can just waltz right in to the castle?
column6: 所以我们可以大摇大摆地直接进城堡？

column5: Yeah.
column6: 对。

column5: Isn't that a little dangerous?
column6: 那不是有点危险吗？

column5: For us and the outsiders, yeah.\nRemember where we are, Valessa.\nDraycu could kill anybody in the blink of an eye.
column6: 对我们和外来者来说，是的。\n记住我们在什么地方，瓦莱莎。\n德雷库眨眼之间就能杀掉任何人。

column5: Letting in people from the mainland is no threat at all.\nAny threat to Alarinthian soil comes from Alarinthia itself.\nOf course, that brings about its own host of problems.
column6: 放大陆上来的人进来根本算不上威胁。\n对阿拉林西亚土地的任何威胁都来自阿拉林西亚自身。\n当然，这也带来了一系列自己的问题。

column5: Wow, you sure know a lot about this stuff.
column6: 哇，你对这些东西懂得真多。

column5: Unfortunately.
column6: 遗憾的是，确实如此。

column5: Whoa, I've never seen this kind of tree before.\nIt's looks really cool! What is it, Ulric?
column6: 哇，我以前从没见过这种树。\n看起来真酷！这是什么，乌尔里克？

column5: It's a pain. They're too thin and weak to be useful.\nAll they can do is provide shade, but even that's weak.\nHiding from the heat in this place is pretty much impossible.
column6: 麻烦得很。它们又细又弱，派不上什么用场。\n唯一的作用就是遮阴，可连这也弱得很。\n想在这地方躲开酷热，基本不可能。

column5: So you can't climb them then, either?
column6: 那也就是说你爬不了它们？

column5: No, I wouldn't advise that.\nThey'd break, and you'd fall to the ground.\nI don't want to play doctor, so just stay away.
column6: 对，我不建议那么做。\n它们会断，你会摔到地上。\n我可不想当医生，所以离远点。

column5: Right, right. Thanks Ulric.
column6: 好，好。谢了，乌尔里克。

column5: Hey, what are you doing!?
column6: 嘿，你在干什么！？

column5: Oh, nothing! Nothing at all!
column6: 哦，没什么！一点事都没有！

column5: I just told you to stay away from those things!\nCome on, Fortaime, you're smarter than that.
column6: 我刚才才跟你说离那些东西远点！\n得了吧，福泰姆，你没那么蠢。

column5: They sure gave us a good ship.\nI have to say, that alliance was a great idea.
column6: 他们确实给了我们一艘好船。\n不得不说，那个联盟是个好主意。

column5: This is an impressive vessel?
column6: 这就算一艘了不起的船了？

column5: Of course. It's amazing.
column6: 当然了。它棒极了。

column5: That is underwhelming.\nThe Monarchy had much bigger vessels.\nWe simply assumed that the pirates held back.
column6: 这让人有些失望。\n君主国曾有比这大得多的船舰。\n我们只是以为海盗们留了一手。

column5: Oh...
Of course, we do not wish to condescend.\nWe only wish to inform you of this world's past.\nSurely that is something that interests you?
column6: 当然，我们无意居高临下。\n我们只是想让你了解这个世界的过去。\n想必那会是你感兴趣的东西吧？

column5: Oh, well when you put it that way — sure.\nSorry, I thought you were rubbing it in my face.
column6: 哦，既然你这么说——那好吧。\n抱歉，我还以为你是故意在挖苦我。

column5: Only partly.
column6: 只有一部分是。

column5: So what're these boxes for?
column6: 那这些箱子是干什么用的？

column5: I'm not sure. Probably food and supplies.\nIt's a long trek to Alarinthia. You need sustenance.
column6: 我不确定。大概是食物和补给吧。\n去阿拉林西亚路途遥远，需要补给。

column5: Oh, then where's our sustenance?
column6: 哦，那我们的补给呢？

column5: I think we went through most of it on the voyage.
column6: 我想大部分都在航行途中用掉了。

column5: Oh no! Are we gonna be in trouble?
column6: 哎呀！我们会有麻烦吗？

column5: Probably.
column6: 大概吧。

column5: What!? Oh, wait...\nYou're joking, aren't you?
column6: 什么！？哦，等等……\n你在开玩笑，对吧？

column5: Probably.
column6: 大概吧。

column5: I need to thank you again, Pommy.\nYour support means a lot to me. It truly does.\nSome of the rebels have started to side with Howl.
column6: 我得再次感谢你，波米。\n你的支持对我意义重大，真的。\n有些反抗军成员已经开始站到豪尔那边了。

column5: A pretty dumb decision, if you ask me.\nI know what they're thinking — that {i}you're{/i} responsible.\nBut that's impossible. Nobody could've seen what was coming.
column6: 要我说，这决定挺蠢的。\n我知道他们在想什么——觉得{i}你{/i}该负责。\n但那不可能。没人能预见到会发生什么。

column5: Yeah, we were played. Caught off guard.\nI know it won't happen again, though. Things are different.\nIt's almost like our belief in the spirit realm was holding us back.
column6: 是啊，我们被耍了。被打了个措手不及。\n不过我知道这种事不会再发生了。情况不一样了。\n就好像我们对灵界的信仰一直在拖累我们。

column5: Do you think the people will even believe us, though?\nI mean, do {i}you{/i} even believe the truth we've been told?
column6: 不过，你觉得大家会相信我们吗？\n我是说，你{i}自己{/i}相信我们被告知的真相吗？

column5: I don't really have a choice, Damek.\nYour speech gave us proof. It was undeniable.\nI'd advise doing the same thing to every other Alestian.
column6: 我其实没得选，达梅克。\n你的演讲给了我们证据。那是无可否认的。\n我建议对每一个阿莱斯提亚人都这么做。

column5: Even if it takes years, you can do it.\nI'll even help you if you need assistance.\nNobody said that things would be easy after the war.
column6: 就算要花上几年，你也能做到。\n如果你需要帮助，我甚至会帮你。\n没人说过战后一切会变得轻松。

column5: You're right, and thanks for that offer. \nI'm pretty sure I'll take you up on it — since this is a tall order.\nBut I know that almost {i}anything{/i} is possible, if we all band together.
column6: 你说得对，谢谢你的提议。\n我很确定我会接受——毕竟这是件艰巨的任务。\n但我知道，只要我们团结一致，几乎{i}任何事{/i}都有可能。

column5: Of course. So for now, we need to fix the discord in our ranks.\nI'll talk with the rebels that are siding with Howl. They need to stop.\nThere {i}are{/i} no sides in this. We all fight for the same cause.
column6: 当然。所以眼下，我们得解决队伍里的分歧。\n我会去跟那些站到豪尔那边的反抗军谈谈。他们得停下来。\n这件事里{i}没有{/i}派系之分。我们都在为同一个目标而战。

column5: And if they put their differences aside?\nWell, Damek? We'll win this thing for sure.
column6: 那如果他们放下分歧呢？\n怎么样，达梅克？我们一定能赢下这场仗。

column5: Halin, Sovy and Shane had finally arrived in Balteus.{w}\nMaking their way to the castle, Sovy trembled with anxiety.{w}\nHe didn't know how The Triumvirate would react to any of this.
column6: 哈林、索维和肖恩终于抵达了巴尔泰乌斯。{w}\n前往城堡的路上，索维紧张得发抖。{w}\n他不知道三人执政团会如何应对这一切。

column5: Halin, can I talk to you for a moment?
column6: 哈林，我能跟你谈一会儿吗？

column5: Of course, Master.
column6: 当然，主人。

column5: They stop in their tracks, Shane included.{w}\nHe knew enough not to intrude on their secret talks.{w}\nHe stood to the side, even though he was now \"one of them\".
column6: 他们停下脚步，肖恩也是。{w}\n他很懂事，没有打扰他们的密谈。{w}\n他站到一旁，尽管他现在已经是“他们中的一员”了。

column5: Back in Mazeo, I was confident. But not anymore.\nI'm starting to worry that The Triumvirate will chastise me.\nWhat should I expect? And how should I react if they do...?
column6: 在马泽奥的时候我还很自信。但现在不是了。\n我开始担心三人执政团会斥责我。\n我该做何准备？如果他们真斥责我，我又该如何应对……？

column5: You act as if you haven't failed them before.
column6: 你表现得好像你从没让他们失望过似的。

column5: Hmm...?
Remember when I first became your Apprentice?\nThey thought you weren't teaching me good enough.\nYou almost went insane when they gave you \"time off\".
column6: 还记得我刚成为你的学徒的时候吗？\n他们觉得你教得不够好。\n他们让你“休假”的时候，你差点疯了。

column5: You would too, Halin. Trust me — it's boring.\nBut that's nothing in comparison to what happened.\nWe don't have the blade, and almost everybody escaped.
column6: 你也会的，哈林。相信我——那很无聊。\n但跟发生的事比起来，那根本不算什么。\n我们没拿到那把剑，而且几乎所有人都逃掉了。

column5: Through no fault of our own, remember?\nI have your back in this. I won't tell them the truth.\nHowever, I need to ask for {i}one{/i} thing in exchange.
column6: 那不是我们的错，记得吗？\n这件事我支持你。我不会告诉他们真相。\n不过，作为交换，我要求{i}一{/i}件事。

column5: Of course.
column6: 当然。

column5: Work on your personal issues, Master.\nI don't care what they are. Just get them sorted out.\nRemember, I'm likely to get chastised just as much as you.
column6: 处理好你的私人问题，主人。\n我不在乎是什么问题。把它们解决掉就行。\n记住，我很可能和你一样会被斥责。

column5: But we'll save the bad news for last.\nWe dealt a major blow to The Rebellion, Sovy.\nWith the loss of their leader, they'll be in disarray.
column6: 但我们会把坏消息留到最后说。\n我们给了反抗军重重一击，索维。\n失去了领袖，他们会陷入混乱。

column5: If The Triumvirate doesn't like that — then it's their problem.\nLike you said, this isn't the last time we'll face them in battle.\nWhether it takes us days or months to win, it shouldn't matter.
column6: 如果三人执政团不满意——那是他们的问题。\n就像你说的，这不是我们最后一次在战场上与他们交锋。\n赢下这场仗要花几天还是几个月，都不重要。

column5: After all, we'll still win.\nWith that said, are we clear?
column6: 毕竟，我们终会赢的。\n话说到这，我们达成一致了吗？

column5: In this moment, it seemed like Halin was the one giving orders.{w}\nHowever, Sovy had no choice but to obey. He couldn't risk being exposed.
column6: 这一刻，看起来发号施令的人反而是哈林。{w}\n然而，索维别无选择，只能服从。他不能冒被揭穿的风险。

column5: We're clear. Let's continue walking.\nI'll think of what to tell them as we move along.
column6: 我们达成一致了。继续走吧。\n路上我会想想该怎么跟他们说。

column5: They break their huddle, and continue walking toward their HQ.{w}\nShane steps closer, striding in unison with Sovy as they do so.
column6: 他们结束密谈，继续朝总部走去。{w}\n肖恩走近了些，与索维并肩同行。

column5: So what was that all about...?\nYou said I was one of you now, right?\nWhen will you start treating me that way?
column6: 那刚才是怎么回事……？\n你说过我现在是你们中的一员，对吧？\n你什么时候才会那样对待我？

column5: Oh, sorry — force of habit.\nWe were just talking about what we should tell our Masters.\nWhile we did damage The Rebellion, we failed in our objective.
column6: 哦，抱歉——习惯了。\n我们只是在商量该跟我们的主子们说些什么。\n虽然我们确实打击了反抗军，但我们没能达成目标。

column5: You mean that blade?
column6: 你是指那把剑？

column5: Yes, and The Seer.
column6: 是的，还有先知。

column5: Yes, and The Seeress.
column6: 是的，还有先知。

column5: Look, Sovy — you kind of saved my life.\nFor that reason alone, you have my support.\nWhatever you want me to do, just let me know.
column6: 听着，索维——你算是救了我的命。\n仅凭这一点，我就支持你。\n不管你想让我做什么，尽管告诉我。

column5: Sovy smiles, having the support of his comrades.{w}\nAny fears he had of being punished, were quickly put to rest.{w}
column6: 索维笑了，他得到了同伴们的支持。{w}\n他之前对被惩罚的种种恐惧，很快就烟消云散了。{w}

column5: Thank you Shane, it means a lot.\nI can tell we're going to get along just fine.
column6: 谢谢你，肖恩，这对我意义重大。\n我看得出来我们会相处得很好。

column5: We take slow, heavy steps through the deserts of Alarinthia.{w}\nHeat assaults us, and the humidity is thick, like sheets in the air.{w}\nUlric seems unfazed, but everyone else is handling it pretty badly.
column6: 我们迈着缓慢沉重的步伐穿过阿拉林西亚的沙漠。{w}\n热浪袭来，湿气浓重，像一层层帷幕悬在空中。{w}\n乌尔里克似乎毫不在意，但其他人都快撑不住了。

column5: I can't believe that people actually {i}live{/i} here.\nHow much farther is it, Ulric? This is crazy.
column6: 我真不敢相信居然有人{i}住在{/i}这里。\n还有多远，乌尔里克？这太疯狂了。

column5: I'd say around six to eight hours.\nThere's an oasis halfway there. We can stop.\nI have a feeling you've already exhausted your canteen.
column6: 大概六到八个小时吧。\n半路有个绿洲。我们可以停下来。\n我感觉你的水壶已经喝空了。

column5: It was too hard to resist.\nSo, there's an oasis in a few hours?\nThat'll be a good place to rest and relax.
column6: 实在太难忍住了。\n那么，几个小时后有个绿洲？\n那是个休息放松的好地方。

column5: We can't waste that kind of time, Damek.\nThere's enough time to fill up on water. That's it.\nIf we take too long, we'll miss both Vivien, and the ball.
column6: 我们不能浪费那么多时间，达梅克。\n只够灌满水。就这样。\n如果我们拖太久，就会错过薇薇安和舞会。

column5: Right. Of course.
column6: 对。当然。

column5: Damek pants, sweat trailing through his fur.{w}\nHe's not alone, though. Almost everybody acts the same.{w}\nHopefully things would cool down once the sun started to set.
column6: 达梅克喘着粗气，汗水顺着他的毛发流淌。{w}\n不过他不是一个人。几乎每个人都一个样。{w}\n希望太阳落山后能凉快一些。

column5: I move toward Ulric as we walk through the desert.{w}\nHe was our guide, so I shouldn't let him out of sight.{w}\nI can see the city in the distance, but no oasis at all.
column6: 穿过沙漠时，我朝乌尔里克走去。{w}\n他是我们的向导，我不该让他离开视线。{w}\n我能看见远处的城市，却根本看不到什么绿洲。

column5: Back in the day, they used these deserts as punishment.\nCriminals were sent out here, and they had to prove their worth.\nIf they were strong enough to survive, then they'd be taken back in.
column6: 从前，他们把这些沙漠当作惩罚之地。\n罪犯被流放到这里，必须证明自己的价值。\n如果他们够强，能活下来，就会被重新接纳。

column5: Most of the time, the criminals would just succumb to the heat.\nThey'd be unable to move, then they'd pass out. Death would come soon after.\nThey called these people \"sixers\", since they usually passed out within six hours.
column6: 大多数时候，罪犯们直接就被酷热击垮了。\n他们会动弹不得，然后昏厥。死亡很快就会降临。\n他们把这种人叫做“六时人”，因为他们通常在六个小时内就会昏倒。

column5: I'm not sure why he's telling this to me.{w}\nIf he wants to pep me up, he's sure failing.\nWe'd be out here for more than six hours.
column6: 我不明白他为什么要跟我说这些。{w}\n如果他是想给我打气，那肯定是失败了。\n我们要在这外面待上超过六个小时。

column5: In addition to that, their bodies lasted six days.\nDon't worry though, we'll be fine. We have water.\nThat isn't a courtesy they wanted to give to criminals.
column6: 除此之外，他们的尸体能撑六天。\n不过别担心，我们会没事的。我们有水。\n那可算不上他们愿意给罪犯的优待。

column5: Well, at least that makes me feel better.
column6: 好吧，至少这让我感觉好点了。

column5: You're probably wondering why I'm telling you this story.
column6: 你大概在想我为什么要给你讲这个故事。

column5: He smiles, and holds out his arm.{w}\nRotating it slightly, he shows off his tattoos.
column6: 他笑了笑，伸出手臂。{w}\n微微转动，展示着他的纹身。

column5: If the \"sixer\" survived, they gave them special markings.\nThey were pardoned, and to be respected for their power.\nA bit of a secret, you know. Just keep it between us, alright?
column6: 如果“六时人”活了下来，他们就会被赐予特殊的印记。\n他们会被赦免，并因自身的力量而受人尊敬。\n算是个小秘密，你知道的。就我们俩知道，行吗？

column5: Wait, so Ulric is an Alarinthian criminal...?{w}\nOr at least he was, since he appears to have been pardoned.{w}\nI'm glad that he was comfortable enough to tell me this kind of stuff.
column6: 等等，所以乌尔里克是阿拉林西亚的罪犯……？{w}\n至少曾经是，因为他似乎已经被赦免了。{w}\n我很高兴他能放心地跟我说这些事。

column5: Besides — they look pretty good, don't they?
column6: 再说——它们挺好看的，对吧？

column5: Well, they haven't used that method of punishment in a while.\nYou might just need to find a copycat artist, like Salus did.\nIf something looks cool, people always try to rip it off.
column6: 嗯，他们已经有一阵子没用那种惩罚方式了。\n你可能得找个模仿的纹身师，就像萨卢斯那样。\n只要什么东西看起来酷，人们总会想模仿。

column5: You're definitely not the first one to say that.\nI didn't like them at first, but they grew on me.\nIf something makes you look better — embrace it.
column6: 你绝对不是第一个这么说的人。\n我一开始也不喜欢它们，但后来渐渐爱上了。\n只要什么东西能让你更好看——就接受它。

column5: Does this make me a different person somehow?\nThere's plenty you haven't told me about {i}your{/i} past.\nYou're still The Monarch to me, and I'm still your friend.
column6: 这难道就让我变成另一个人了吗？\n关于{i}你{/i}的过去，也有很多你没告诉我的事。\n对我来说你依然是君主，我也依然是你的朋友。

column5: I'd say good luck, but they don't do \"sixers\" anymore.\nThey stopped that method of punishment ages ago.\nYou might need to find a copycat on the black market.
column6: 我本想祝你好运，但他们已经不搞“六时人”了。\n他们很久以前就废止了那种惩罚方式。\n你可能得去黑市找个模仿者。

column5: Well, I guess they're not for everybody.\nI think I'd look a bit bland without them, you know?\nWe could all benefit from some \"embellishment\".
column6: 嗯，我猜它们不是人人都适合。\n我觉得没有它们我会显得有点平淡，你懂吗？\n我们都能从一些“点缀”中受益。

column5: Anyway, I guess that's enough story time for now.\nThe more you know about Alarinthia, the better.\nThat, and it makes the walk go by way faster.
column6: 总之，我想故事时间到此为止吧。\n你对阿拉林西亚了解得越多越好。\n而且，这能让路程走得快得多。

column5: If you'll excuse me, I have some business to take care of.\nWe'll have plenty of time to talk later, [firstname]. Trust me.\nIf you find that you're needing anything, just wave me down.
column6: 恕我失陪，我有些事要处理。\n以后我们有的是时间聊，[firstname]。相信我。\n如果你需要什么，朝我挥挥手就行。

column5: I nod, before looking back at the rest of my comrades.{w}\nThey look so drained, and fatigued. We need that oasis, and fast.
column6: 我点点头，然后回头看向其余的同伴。{w}\n他们看起来筋疲力尽，疲惫不堪。我们急需那个绿洲。

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: From what I've experienced so far? It's awful.\nI'm holding out on the hope that it's colder in the city.\nBut I know that won't be true. I bet it'll be even worse.
column6: 就我目前的体验？糟透了。\n我一直盼着城里会凉快点。\n但我知道那不可能。我打赌只会更糟。

column5: If I lived here, I'd definitely be nocturnal.\nI mean, it must get colder at night time, right?\nI'd just sleep the day away — and that's a fact.
column6: 如果我住在这里，肯定会变成夜行动物。\n我是说，晚上总会凉快点，对吧？\n我就白天睡大觉——这是肯定的。

column5: So I guess not much would change, to be honest.\nThough I haven't been able to get much sleep lately.\nAnyway, yeah — it's basically the worst place in the world.
column6: 所以老实说，我想也不会有什么改变。\n不过最近我一直睡不好。\n总之，是啊——这基本就是世界上最糟的地方。

column5: I sure hope so, otherwise this would be a waste.\nI mean, coming here, and then leaving empty handed?\nThat'd mean we put ourselves through all of this for nothing.
column6: 我希望如此，否则这趟就白来了。\n我是说，大老远跑来，然后空手而归？\n那意味着我们白受了这么多苦。

column5: That's not my style, you know.\nI don't care if we have to fight in a tournament, even.\nWe're not coming all the way here only to accomplish nothing.
column6: 那可不是我的风格，你知道的。\n就算要参加比武大会我也无所谓。\n我们大老远跑来，绝不是为了白跑一趟。

column5: Whoa, putting me on the spot, huh?\nI guess I'd probably side with Vivien.\nUlric hates this place, and I can see why.
column6: 哇，你这是当众考我啊？\n我想我大概会站在薇薇安这边。\n乌尔里克讨厌这个地方，我明白为什么。

column5: Politics would only make this a million times worse.\nSo I think Alarinthia would be better off like the mainland.\nIt's different, yes. But in my opinion, it's a {i}bad{/i} different.
column6: 政治只会让这里糟糕一百万倍。\n所以我觉得阿拉林西亚还是像大陆那样比较好。\n是不一样，没错。但在我看来，是{i}糟糕的{/i}不一样。

column5: Like, Mazeo was different, but it was {i}good{/i}.\nA constant battle to see who is stronger? Yikes.\nSounds like that would get pretty toxic, and fast.
column6: 比如，马泽奥也不一样，但那是{i}好的{/i}不一样。\n不断地比谁更强？啧。\n听起来很快就会变得相当恶劣。

column5: That's a tough choice, but I'd have to say Damek.\nIt's not fair that Howl tried to pin all of this on him.\nNothing that happened at the Rebel HQ was his fault.
column6: 这选择挺难的，但我得说是达梅克。\n豪尔想把这一切都推到他身上，这太不公平了。\n反抗军总部发生的事没有一件是他的错。

column5: But that doesn't mean I hate Howl. Far from it.\nHe seems so wise, and we could learn a lot from him.\nAn entire ancient culture inside of him? Just think about it.
column6: 但这不代表我讨厌豪尔。差得远呢。\n他看起来那么有智慧，我们能从他身上学到很多。\n他体内装着整个古老的文化？想想看吧。

column5: There's so much we don't know about The Monarchy.\nHe could help us fill dozens and dozens of history books.\nI hope he survives this. He has {i}lots{/i} of info to pass on to us.
column6: 关于君主国，我们不知道的太多了。\n他能帮我们写满几十本历史书。\n我希望他能活下来。他有{i}很多{/i}信息要传给我们。

column5: No, and I'm slowly melting.\nI went through all my water within the first hours.\nMy fault, I know. I'll make sure to ration it better next time.
column6: 不，我正慢慢融化呢。\n头几个小时我就把水全喝光了。\n是我的错，我知道。下次我一定好好分配。

column5: If there is a next time, of course.\nI'm starting to think that this oasis was a lie.\nI see mirages, sure, but no {i}real{/i} water.
column6: 当然了，如果有下次的话。\n我开始觉得这个绿洲是个骗局。\n我确实看到了海市蜃楼，但没有{i}真正的{/i}水。

column5: If you see it, make sure to tell me right away.\nI might even go for a swim if I have the time.\nYou should join me. It'd be pretty awesome.
column6: 如果你看到了，一定要马上告诉我。\n要是有时间，我甚至可能去游个泳。\n你也一起来吧。那会很棒的。

column5: Hey Pro, can I talk to you for a second?
column6: 嘿，普洛，能跟你聊一下吗？

column5: Of course! What's up?
column6: 当然！怎么了？

column5: I can't say in front of everybody else.\nI need to talk to you alone. In {i}secret{/i}.
column6: 我不能当着大家的面说。\n我需要单独跟你谈。{i}私下{/i}谈。

column5: Oh, is it about {i}that{/i}?
column6: 哦，是{i}那件事{/i}吗？

column5: Pro. Not in front of anybody else.\nFollow me over here, and talk quietly.
column6: 普洛。别当着别人的面说。\n跟我到这边来，说话小声点。

column5: Right, right. Sorry.\nWell then, what's up?
column6: 好，好。抱歉。\n那么，怎么了？

column5: Sand, sand, and more sand.{w}\nWait, what's that? Right. Sand.
column6: 沙子，沙子，还是沙子。{w}\n等等，那是什么？对。沙子。

column5: These cliffs must act as landmarks.{w}\nWithout those, it would be easy to get lost.{w}\nGetting lost in this desert could easily be deadly.
column6: 这些悬崖一定充当了地标。{w}\n没有它们，很容易迷路。{w}\n在这片沙漠里迷路，很容易就会送命。

column5: I guess that's Alarinthia, way out there.{w}\nThis is going to be one {i}long{/i} journey.{w}\nHopefully the oasis helps all of us out.
column6: 我猜那就是阿拉林西亚，在很远的地方。{w}\n这将是一趟{i}漫长{/i}的旅程。{w}\n希望那个绿洲能帮到我们大家。

column5: These cliffs must act as landmarks.{w}\nWithout those, it would be easy to get lost.{w}\nGetting lost in this desert could easily be deadly.
column6: 这些悬崖一定充当了地标。{w}\n没有它们，很容易迷路。{w}\n在这片沙漠里迷路，很容易就会送命。

column5: When we arrive at the oasis, everybody immediately runs toward it.{w}\nOpening their canteens, they fill them up, and quickly drink up.{w}\nI do the same, before turning to face my allies in relief.
column6: 到达绿洲时，所有人立刻朝它跑去。{w}\n他们打开水壶，灌满水，然后一饮而尽。{w}\n我也照做，然后如释重负地转向我的同伴们。

column5: I was starting to get parched, and worried about passing out.{w}\nThe placement of an oasis here was awfully convenient.{w}\nI choose not to count our blessings, as I face my friends.
column6: 我开始口干舌燥，担心会昏倒。{w}\n这里正好有个绿洲，未免也太方便了。{w}\n面对朋友们时，我选择不去细想这份幸运。

column5: This is amazing! Just what I needed!\nIf you don't mind, I'm gonna take a swim.\nJust give me a few minutes, alright...?
column6: 太棒了！正是我需要的！\n如果你不介意，我要去游个泳。\n就给我几分钟，行吗……？

column5: Fortaime, no! That's disgusting.\nPeople drink this water. It's not for swimming.
column6: 福泰姆，不行！那太恶心了。\n人们要喝这水。不是用来游泳的。

column5: But!
column6: 可是！

column5: No!
column6: 不行！

column5: Fortaime scoffs, and crosses his arms.{w}\nThis is the moment I decide to tell them what Howl told me.{w}\nWithout the power from Sauleberg's idol, Valinorth would be fine.
column6: 福泰姆嗤了一声，抱起双臂。{w}\n就在这一刻，我决定把豪尔告诉我的事告诉他们。{w}\n没有索尔伯格灵像的力量，瓦利诺斯也会安然无恙。

column5: Wait, really!?
column6: 等等，真的吗！？

column5: That's amazing...!\nAnd you're certain about this?
column6: 太不可思议了……！\n你确定吗？

column5: I nod. Howl was definitely a reliable source.{w}\nThere was now an upside to all of our shaken faith.
column6: 我点点头。豪尔绝对是个可靠的消息来源。{w}\n如今，我们那动摇的信仰也算有了个好处。

column5: I totally needed to hear some good news!\nThis trek through the desert is downright awful.\nWhen we get back, let's all go back to Valinorth!
column6: 我太需要听到点好消息了！\n这趟穿越沙漠的跋涉简直糟透了。\n等我们回去，大家一起回瓦利诺斯吧！

column5: Yeah, definitely! It'll feel so good to be back home.\nWith your vision, and that dim idol, my outlook was so grim.\nBut now that attack won't happen, and the idol doesn't matter.
column6: 是啊，当然！回到家的感觉一定很棒。\n再加上你的幻象和那黯淡的灵像，我本来一片悲观。\n但现在那场袭击不会发生了，灵像也无所谓了。

column5: Long live Valinorth...?
column6: 瓦利诺斯万岁……？

column5: Long live Valinorth.
column6: 瓦利诺斯万岁。

column5: We all smile before parting ways. I look over at Ulric and Pro.{w}\nThey're talking to each other, but very quietly. Almost secretive.{w}\nI choose not to interrupt them and make my way over to Damek.
column6: 我们相视一笑，然后各自散去。我看向乌尔里克和普洛。{w}\n他们正在交谈，但声音很低。几乎像是在密谋。{w}\n我选择不去打扰他们，径直走向达梅克。

column5: Hey, we were just talking about our future options.\nI mean, would we rather side with Vivien or Draycu?\nI think Vivien is the better option, but Howl disagrees.
column6: 嘿，我们刚在讨论我们未来的选择。\n我是说，我们该站在薇薇安还是德雷库那边？\n我觉得薇薇安是更好的选择，但豪尔不同意。

column5: As we seem to do on many matters.\nWe need strength to win the upcoming war, Damek.\nVivien cannot deliver as much strength. Only hope for her nation.
column6: 就像我们在许多事上那样。\n我们需要力量来赢下即将到来的战争，达梅克。\n薇薇安提供不了那么多力量。只能给她的人民希望。

column5: If hope could win wars, we wouldn't even be here.\nIn times like this, we are glad that you're not in charge.\nWe trust that the Monarch will make the proper decision.
column6: 如果希望就能打赢战争，我们根本就不会在这里。\n在这种时候，我们很庆幸掌权的不是你。\n我们相信君主会做出正确的决定。

column5: Well, what do you say, Monarch?\nIf you had to choose right now, what would you do?\nJust a hypothetical of course. Nothing set in stone.
column6: 那么，你怎么说，君主？\n如果你现在必须做选择，你会怎么做？\n当然只是假设。没有定论。

column5: There you have it, Howl.\nWe need to think about the future of this world, too.\nIt makes sense to give Alarinthia a new form of leadership.
column6: 你也听到了，豪尔。\n我们也得为这个世界的未来着想。\n给阿拉林西亚一种新的领导方式，是合情合理的。

column5: Aww, really...? Come on, Monarch.\nI know we need strength, but we need to think about Alestia.\nWe have the chance to reshape an entire nation, here.
column6: 啊，真的吗……？拜托，君主。\n我知道我们需要力量，但我们得为阿莱斯提亚考虑。\n我们有机会重塑一整个国家。

column5: There is nothing wrong with the way Alarinthia is run.\nYou cannot change it simply because you do not like it.\nSuch a move would make you no better than The Triumvirate.
column6: 阿拉林西亚的统治方式没有任何问题。\n你不能仅仅因为自己不喜欢就去改变它。\n那样做只会让你和三人执政团没什么两样。

column5: We cannot become the enemy we seek to dethrone.\nYour way of thinking requires some reevaluation, Damek.\nYou may say \"means to an end\", but so does The Triumvirate.
column6: 我们不能变成我们想要推翻的敌人。\n你的想法需要重新审视，达梅克。\n你或许会说“为达目的不择手段”，但三人执政团也是这么想的。

column5: Wow, you paint me as such a villain.
column6: 哇，你把我描绘得像个大反派。

column5: A change in leadership would require the spilling of blood.\nInnocents would die, much like the occupation of Mazeo.\nThink of what you lost. Do you want to do this to others?
column6: 更换领导层需要流血。\n无辜者会死去，就像马泽奥被占领时那样。\n想想你失去的一切。你想对别人做同样的事吗？

column5: Damek seems unable to come up with a response to this.{w}\nPromptly changing the subject, he seems to admit defeat.
column6: 达梅克似乎无法回应这番话。{w}\n他马上转移了话题，看来是认输了。

column5: Well, are you all full up on water...?\nUlric said we're halfway there, and we're making good time.\nI think we'll make it to the city with plenty of time to spare, Monarch.
column6: 那么，你们的水都灌满了吗……？\n乌尔里克说我们走了一半了，进度不错。\n我想我们能提前不少时间赶到城里，君主。

column5: Howl seems unamused at the sudden change in topic.
column6: 豪尔对这突如其来的话题转变似乎并不买账。

column5: This body does not work like you would expect.\nWe do not need water, and do not risk passing out.\nWhenever you're ready to continue, we will do so.
column6: 这具身体不像你想象的那样运作。\n我们不需要水，也不会昏倒。\n你们准备好继续时，我们就出发。

column5: After saying that, we all part ways.{w}\nWe shouldn't stay here for too much longer.{w}\nMissing that ball would damage our cause immensely.
column6: 说完这些，我们各自散开。{w}\n我们不该在这里停留太久。{w}\n错过那场舞会对我们的事业将是巨大的打击。

column5: I could sit here and drink this all day.\nI've never missed water so much in my entire life.\nIn fact, leave me behind. I'll stay here until things are done.
column6: 我可以坐在这儿，一整天都喝这个。\n我这辈子从没这么想念过水。\n其实，把我留下吧。我会待在这里，直到事情办完。

column5: Nice try, but you're not getting out of this {i}that{/i} easy.\nFill up your canteen, Fortaime. We need to get going.
column6: 想得美，可你不会{i}那么{/i}容易就逃掉。\n把水壶灌满，福泰姆。我们得出发了。

column5: Wait, your canteen is so much bigger than mine.\nCan we trade...? You're used to this desert, Ulric.
column6: 等等，你的水壶比我的大多了。\n我们换一下行吗……？你习惯这片沙漠了，乌尔里克。

column5: Used to it...? I haven't been here for thou—\nYou know what? Fine, you can have it, Fortaime.\nJust fill it up and let's get going, okay?
column6: 习惯……？我都几千年没来这——\n算了吧。行，给你，福泰姆。\n把它灌满，我们走，行吗？

column5: Alright. Score!
column6: 好吧。赚到了！

column5: Fortaime circles these trees. Clearly, he wants to climb them.{w}\nIt's not very long until Ulric grabs him and takes him away.{w}\nHe's almost become some sort of babysitter at this rate.
column6: 福泰姆绕着这些树打转。显然，他想爬上去。{w}\n没过多久，乌尔里克就把他抓住带走了。{w}\n照这样下去，他简直快成保姆了。

column5: Still no sign of the city. How much farther could it be...?{w}\nI think Ulric said this was the halfway point, or something.{w}\nHopefully none of us pass out from exhaustion in this place.
column6: 还是看不到城市的影子。到底还有多远……？{w}\n我记得乌尔里克说这里是半途，还是别的什么。{w}\n希望我们没人会在这地方累昏过去。

column5: This banter appears because of your choice to create Seers.
column6: 这段闲聊出现，是因为你选择了创造先知。

column5: So, what's it like to be a Seer...?\nWhat kind of stuff are you starting to see?\nDoes it hurt your head? Are you enjoying it...?
column6: 那么，当先知是什么感觉……？\n你开始看到什么样的东西了？\n会头疼吗？你喜欢这种感觉吗……？

column5: It gives me great pleasure to see the future.\nBut right now, it's just little things. Indecipherable.\nPerhaps as we process this, things will become clearer.
column6: 能看到未来让我非常欣喜。\n但眼下只是些小事。难以解读。\n也许随着我们逐渐适应，一切会变得更清晰。

column5: I see loss in the future. Loss, and tragedy.\nBut for which side of this battle, I cannot say.\nIt seems to be a \"gut feeling\", at the moment.
column6: 我在未来看到了失去。失去，还有悲剧。\n但属于这场战斗的哪一方，我说不上来。\n眼下，这更像是一种“直觉”。

column5: Yeah, it's the same for me. Brief flashes.\nBut I see a coliseum, and a big struggle.\nI think you'll all be fighting during your visit.
column6: 是啊，我也一样。短暂的闪念。\n但我看到了一座斗兽场，还有一场激烈的搏斗。\n我想你们此行的期间会有一场战斗。

column5: Fighting...? That's no fun.\nHopefully your powers get better over time.\nImagine how strong you'd be in those battles...!
column6: 战斗……？那可不好玩。\n希望你们的能力会随着时间变得更强。\n想象一下你们在那些战斗里会有多强……！

column5: Able to see every move before the enemy even makes it.\nWith that power, we'd never have to worry about tragedy or loss.\nI can tell you're going to be one of the best assets in this war.
column6: 能在敌人出手之前就看穿他的每一步。\n有了那种力量，我们就再也不用担心悲剧或牺牲了。\n我看得出来，你们会成为这场战争中最宝贵的战力之一。

column5: Why thank you. That means a lot.\nI'm happy to serve The Rebellion in any way I can.\nWhat they did back in those tunnels was inexcusable.
column6: 哦，谢谢你。这对我意义重大。\n我很乐意尽我所能为反抗军效力。\n他们在那些隧道里做的事不可饶恕。

column5: Yeah. I'd say we show them the same treatment.\nWe'll fight for a future that all of you can enjoy.\nEven if we can't join that future ourselves.
column6: 是啊。要我说，我们该以牙还牙。\n我们会为一个你们所有人都能享受的未来而战。\n哪怕我们自己无法进入那个未来。

column5: That's certainly a pessimistic view, Ignace.\nThere might be a way to save our minds, you know.\nThis Rebellion has proved that {i}anything{/i} is possible.
column6: 这看法确实挺悲观的，伊格纳斯。\n也许有办法保住我们的心智，你知道的。\n这场反抗已经证明了{i}任何事{/i}皆有可能。

column5: Yeah, you're right.\nWe'll make it through this.
column6: 是啊，你说得对。\n我们会挺过去的。

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: I can't believe how hot it is, actually.\nI mean, Ulric told us stories, and I thought he was exaggerating.\nAs soon as we stepped off that ship, I knew he was actually right.
column6: 真不敢相信这里这么热。\n我是说，乌尔里克给我们讲过那些故事，我还以为他在夸张。\n可我们一下船，我就知道他说的都是真的。

column5: Of course, he doesn't seem like the type to embellish his stories.\nMaybe some part of me was just hoping it wouldn't be that bad.\nHe painted such a grim picture of this place, you know...?
column6: 当然，他看起来不像是会添油加醋的那种人。\n也许我心底有一部分只是希望没那么糟。\n他把这地方描述得太可怕了，你知道吧……？

column5: Vivien, hands down. I don't like the way Alarinthia is run.\nRelying on strength alone creates such a toxic atmosphere.\nAnyone with a brilliant mind would simply be pushed aside.
column6: 毫无疑问是薇薇安。我不喜欢阿拉林西亚的统治方式。\n只靠力量维系，会营造出如此恶劣的氛围。\n任何才华横溢的人都会被直接排挤到一边。

column5: That holds back the progression of society by {i}so{/i} much.\nValinorth embraced new ideas, and nurtured bright minds.\nIf anything, it actually explains why Alarinthia is so primitive.
column6: 这{i}大大{/i}阻碍了社会的进步。\n瓦利诺斯拥抱新思想，培育聪慧的头脑。\n真要说的话，这恰好解释了为什么阿拉林西亚如此原始。

column5: It's so weird, seeing our former Elder just walking around.\nBut I need to work on that. I need my mind to {i}know{/i} it's not him.\nSalus is gone, and there's nothing we can do to change that fact.
column6: 看到我们前任长老就这么四处走动，感觉太奇怪了。\n但我得克服这一点。我得让我的脑子{i}明白{/i}那不是他。\n萨卢斯已经走了，我们无法改变这个事实。

column5: Howl is an interesting guy. He sure has a lot to say.\nHis insight into the past of the world could fill a million books.\nWith all of those souls, he knows almost everything there is to know.
column6: 豪尔是个有意思的人。他确实有很多话要说。\n他对这个世界过去的洞见能写满一百万本书。\n凭着那些灵魂，他几乎无所不知。

column5: He told me that society has actually {i}regressed{/i} in Alarinthia.\nIt used to be one with The Monarchy. Their whole world was united.\nI hope we can make a world like that, after this war is finally over.
column6: 他告诉我，阿拉林西亚的社会其实{i}倒退了{/i}。\n它曾经与君主国融为一体。他们的整个世界是统一的。\n希望等这场战争最终结束后，我们能创造那样一个世界。

column5: Yeah, I want to break the record for most water ever ingested.\nI'll never take something like that for granted ever again, I swear.\nIt makes me miss the water tank from back in Valinorth, actually.
column6: 是啊，我想打破喝水最多的纪录。\n我发誓，我再也不会把这种事当成理所当然了。\n说真的，这让我开始想念瓦利诺斯的水箱了。

column5: Whenever we needed it, it was right there on demand.\nOne oasis in the entire desert makes water pretty scarce.\nHow do they handle the water situation in their capital...?
column6: 我们需要的时候，它随时都在。\n整片沙漠只有一处绿洲，水就变得相当稀缺。\n他们的首都是怎么解决用水问题的……？

column5: Yeah, I think he'll be fine. It's just a lot to take in.\nHe finally has a chance to change this place for the better.\nApparently that's all he's wanted ever since he was young.
column6: 是啊，我想他不会有事的。只是要接受的太多了。\n他终于有机会把这里变得更好。\n据说那是他打小就唯一想要的东西。

column5: I feel like this world will be completely different after we win.\nThat's such a scary thought. Well, scary and exciting.\nWe're leading a revolution. I almost can't believe it.
column6: 我感觉等我们赢了之后，这个世界会彻底不同。\n这想法真让人害怕。嗯，既害怕又兴奋。\n我们正在引领一场革命。我几乎不敢相信。

column5: We arrive at the gates to Alarinthia, after an exhausting trek through the desert.{w}\nIt feels like things will change now that we're here, but they probably won't.{w}\nThe city won't be any more inviting. There just might be more water.
column6: 在经历了穿越沙漠的艰苦跋涉后，我们抵达了阿拉林西亚的城门。{w}\n感觉到了这里，一切都会改变，但大概并不会。{w}\n这座城市不会更友好。只是也许水会多一些。

column5: A lone man stands at the gates, and I recognize him.{w}\nHe's the man I saw watching us back at the docks.{w}\nThis can't be coincidence. He must be after us.
column6: 城门口站着一个孤身男子，我认出了他。{w}\n他就是我在码头时看到监视我们的那个人。{w}\n这不可能是巧合。他一定是在追我们。

column5: Ulric notices him and starts to walk toward the gate.
column6: 乌尔里克注意到了他，开始朝城门走去。

column5: Let me handle this, I've been here before.\nHe probably knows who we are. Info travels fast, here.\nJust stay calm, and I'll have us in the city in no time, alright?
column6: 让我来处理，我以前来过这里。\n他大概知道我们是谁。在这里消息传得很快。\n都别慌，我很快就能让我们进城，行吗？

column5: We all nod, leaving Ulric to handle the situation.
column6: 我们都点点头，让乌尔里克去处理局面。

column5: We seek passage into the city, and nothing more.\nIt's been a long trip from Mazeo, and we need shelter.\nOur business lies with the ones known as Vivien and Draycu.
column6: 我们只求进城，别无所图。\n从马泽奥一路走来路途漫长，我们需要落脚之处。\n我们要找的人是薇薇安和德雷库。

column5: The man remains silent for a few moments, before bursting into laughter.
column6: 那人沉默了片刻，然后突然大笑起来。

column5: I know exactly who you are, Ulric.\nVivien is waiting for you in the tavern.\nAnd Draycu? Well, you'll have a ball to attend.
column6: 我完全知道你是谁，乌尔里克。\n薇薇安正在酒馆里等你。\n至于德雷库？嗯，你还有场舞会要参加。

column5: Wait, how do you know who I am...?
column6: 等等，你怎么知道我是谁……？

column5: I followed you all, up until the oasis.\nThat was my chance to get ahead, and tip off Vivien.\nBesides, you stick out like a sore thumb. Nice markings, \"sixer\".
column6: 我一路跟着你们，直到绿洲那儿。\n那是我抄近路、给薇薇安通风报信的机会。\n再说，你太扎眼了。不错的印记，“六时人”。

column5: I trust that won't be an issue...?
column6: 我想这不会有什么问题吧……？

column5: It shouldn't, but I'm surprised you found somebody to do that.\nRecreating the markings of the ancients is frowned upon.\nThey {i}earned{/i} those markings. You certainly did not.
column6: 应该不会，但我很好奇你居然找到了人给你弄这个。\n重现古人的印记是会遭人唾弃的。\n那些印记是他们{i}挣来的{/i}。你就肯定不是。

column5: Of course.
column6: 当然。

column5: Though you do bear a striking resemblance to the Ulric of legend.\nIf anything, that'll make your relationship with Vivien more amicable.
column6: 不过你确实和传说中的乌尔里克长得出奇地像。\n真要说的话，这会让你们和薇薇安的关系更融洽。

column5: I was given this name by my parents.\nThey aligned with his views, and so do I.\nIf that'll be all, we'd like to keep going.
column6: 这个名字是我父母给我起的。\n他们认同他的理念，我也是。\n如果没有别的事，我们想继续走了。

column5: Of course. I wasn't standing here to stop you.\nI merely wished to welcome you back home.\nI hope you and your \"Monarch\" end up useful.
column6: 当然。我站在这儿不是要拦你们。\n我只是想欢迎你们回家。\n希望你和你的“君主”最后能派上用场。

column5: He bows to Ulric, as a sign of respect.
column6: 他向乌尔里克鞠躬，以示敬意。

column5: By the way. Call me Drakeor.
column6: 顺便说一句。叫我德雷克。

column5: Ulric nods, before turning back to face us.{w}\nDrakeor enters the city, likely returning to Vivien's side.{w}\nI'm glad that our quest in this land finally has some direction.
column6: 乌尔里克点点头，然后转身面向我们。{w}\n德雷克进了城，大概是回到薇薇安身边去了。{w}\n我很高兴我们在这片土地上的任务终于有了方向。

column5: Well, that was easy.\nBecause of the ball, there's almost no security.\nI knew he'd be involved with Vivien. I could just tell.
column6: 嗯，还挺顺利。\n因为舞会的缘故，几乎没有什么守卫。\n我就知道他和薇薇安有牵连。我一眼就看出来了。

column5: So we'll have enough time to meet with her before the ball.\nThat's great, I was worried we'd be on a tight schedule.\nYou can't really rush decisions that change a nation.
column6: 所以我们有足够的时间在舞会前见她。\n太好了，我本来还担心时间会很紧。\n改变一个国家的决定，可急不得。

column5: Yeah, it was definitely fortuitous.\nWe better make sure it's not a trap.\nThat's the perfect way to catch us off guard.
column6: 是啊，这绝对是个巧合的好运。\n我们最好确定这不是个陷阱。\n那可是让我们措手不及的绝佳方式。

column5: Well, he didn't seem disingenuous.
column6: 嗯，他看起来不像是在装假。

column5: That's the perfect way to catch us off guard.
column6: 那可是让我们措手不及的绝佳方式。

column5: Right. So what's the next step?
column6: 对。那下一步是什么？

column5: We head into the town square.\nIf the tavern hasn't moved, it's connected.\nWe'll be seeing Vivien within the hour, for sure.
column6: 我们进城去城镇广场。\n如果酒馆没搬走，它们是相通的。\n一小时内我们肯定能见到薇薇安。

column5: Alright, sounds good to me.\nIs there more water in the city...?
column6: 好，听起来不错。\n城里水更多吗……？

column5: Yeah, but don't ask for water in the tavern.\nIt's seen as a sign of weakness amongst Alarinthians.\nIf you drink anything while we're there, make sure it's ale.
column6: 有，但在酒馆里别要水。\n在阿拉林西亚人看来，那是软弱的表现。\n我们在那儿的时候，你要喝什么，一定得是麦酒。

column5: Everybody stands around, seeming to wait for my mark.{w}\nThere's something up with Ulric, I have a strong gut feeling.{w}\nHis secret talks with Pro, and some of the things Drakeor said.
column6: 大家都站在周围，似乎在等我发号施令。{w}\n我的直觉强烈地告诉我，乌尔里克有事瞒着我们。{w}\n他和普洛的密谈，还有德雷克说的那些话。

column5: Hmm.
column6: 嗯。

column5: No, it is completely different. More primitive.\nAlarinthia existed in unison with The Monarchy.\nIt was one part of a larger whole. It was peaceful.
column6: 不，它完全不同。更加原始。\n阿拉林西亚曾与君主国和谐共存。\n它曾是一个更大整体的一部分。那时很和平。

column5: Being stuck in a constant power struggle sounds awful.\nBut still, it has given us what we need. A strong potential ally.\nDraycu is the result of generations of a savage cycle of growth.
column6: 陷在持续不断的权力斗争中，听起来很可怕。\n但尽管如此，它给了我们需要的东西。一个强大的潜在盟友。\n德雷库是世代野蛮成长循环的产物。

column5: Every ruler, stronger than the last.\nFor almost an eternity, they have followed these laws.\nDraycu and his army must be exceptional in their power.
column6: 每一任统治者都比上一任更强。\n几乎永恒以来，他们都遵循着这些法则。\n德雷库和他的军队的力量一定非同寻常。

column5: We have no complaints.\nIt seems to be others who have problems.\nEspecially those close to Salus, like his son.
column6: 我们没有怨言。\n似乎有意见的是别人。\n尤其是那些与萨卢斯亲近的人，比如他的儿子。

column5: But we will work on that while we travel.\nPerhaps your forces just need time to adjust.\nThis must be a jarring transition, to say the least.
column6: 但我们会在旅途中处理这件事。\n也许你的部下只是需要时间适应。\n至少可以说，这一定是个令人不适的转变。

column5: Yes. We require no sustenance.\nWe may eat and drink with this body, but it is not necessary.\nIf anything, we would do it for pleasure, rather than to survive.
column6: 是的。我们不需要进食。\n这具身体可以吃喝，但没有必要。\n真要说的话，我们吃喝是为了享受，而不是为了生存。

column5: But pleasure is not something we require, either.\nSo, because of that, we choose not to eat or drink.\nThere are those who need it more than us, [firstname].
column6: 但享受也不是我们所必需的。\n所以，正因如此，我们选择不吃不喝。\n有人比我们更需要这些，[firstname]。

column5: We are unable to comment on this matter.\nConjecture of that kind will lead nowhere constructive.\nWe must simply increase our chances of winning — and try.
column6: 我们无法对这件事发表评论。\n那种猜测不会有任何建设性的结果。\n我们只能想方设法提高胜算——然后尽力而为。

column5: This banter appears because of your choice to create Monarch Vessels.
column6: 这段闲聊出现，是因为你选择了创造君主容器。

column5: So what's it like...?\nYou know, being a vessel.
column6: 那是什么感觉……？\n你知道的，成为容器。

column5: It is not much different than when we were alive.\nThere are simply voices in our head. Lots of them.\nThe Monarchy guides our every move.
column6: 跟我们活着的时候没太大区别。\n只是脑海里有声音。很多声音。\n君主国指引着我们的每一个举动。

column5: They are fueled by the rage of their imprisonment.\nEverything inside of us tells us to fight, and to kill.\nWhen the time comes, we will fight for this world.
column6: 他们被囚禁的愤怒所驱动。\n我们内心的一切都叫嚣着要战斗，要杀戮。\n时机到来时，我们会为这个世界而战。

column5: The wounds on our bodies hurt us at first.\nBut like white noise, we have phased it out.\nIt only flares up every few minutes, now.
column6: 起初我们身上的伤口会疼。\n但就像白噪音一样，我们已经逐渐屏蔽了它。\n现在只是每隔几分钟发作一次。

column5: And how bad is it...?
column6: 那有多疼……？

column5: We feel every wound as if freshly inflicted.\nIt is almost like we exist on the edge of life and death.\nOur body is unable to fully commit to either side of the spectrum.
column6: 每一道伤口我们都感觉像是刚受的伤。\n简直就像我们存在于生与死的边缘。\n我们的身体无法完全归属于任何一端。

column5: That sounds horrible...
column6: 听起来太可怕了……

column5: Horrible, yes. But also necessary.\nWith our aid, The Triumvirate shall fall.\nJustice will finally be given to The Monarchy.
column6: 可怕，是的。但也是必要的。\n有我们的相助，三人执政团必将倒下。\n正义终将还给君主国。

column5: When we can deliver that justice, the pain is worth it.\nWe embrace this as a gift, and will honor The Monarch.\nWithout their choice, we would not be alive to fight.
column6: 当我们能带来那份正义时，这痛苦就值得了。\n我们视此为恩赐，并将尊崇君主。\n若不是他们的选择，我们就无法活着战斗。

column5: I just wish there was a way to make the pain go away.\nYou know, after this war, you're still going to suffer.
column6: 我只希望能有办法消除这痛苦。\n你知道的，这场战争之后，你依然会受苦。

column5: We are not the only ones who will continue to suffer.\nThe wounds endured during this war can also be emotional.\nScars will haunt {i}all{/i} of your forces. We are not the only ones.
column6: 会继续受苦的不只是我们。\n这场战争中承受的创伤也可能是情感上的。\n伤疤会困扰你们{i}所有{/i}的部队。我们并不是唯一。

column5: Right...

When we arrive at the docks, we finally get an up close view of everything.{w}\nIt's a massive shipyard, with vessels both arriving and departing.{w}\nPeople run in every direction, a mixture of workers and pirates.
column6: 当我们抵达码头时，终于近距离看到了这一切。{w}\n那是个巨大的船坞，既有船舰进港，也有船舰离港。{w}\n人们朝各个方向奔忙，混着工人和海盗。

column5: I suppose they share the same workspace.{w}\nIt's interesting how I can discern a pirate from their clothes and demeanor.{w}\nAfter a few steps into the shipyard, we're surrounded by tons of people.
column6: 我猜他们共用同一个工作场所。{w}\n有趣的是，我能从衣着和举止分辨出谁是海盗。{w}\n走进船坞没几步，我们就被无数人包围了。

column5: Hey, stick close to me.\nWouldn't want to get lost, right?
column6: 嘿，紧跟着我。\n可不想走丢，对吧？

column5: He inches closer to me, and we make our way through the shipyard.{w}\nIt must be their busy hour or something, because we can barely move.{w}\nPeople bump into us, and apologize before moving on their way.
column6: 他向我靠近了些，我们穿过船坞。{w}\n一定是赶上他们最忙的时候了，因为我们几乎挪不动。{w}\n人们撞到我们，道个歉又继续赶路。

column5: We're heading to that bridge up there.
column6: 我们要去那边那座桥。

column5: He points forward, to a bridge in the distance.{w}\nAt this rate, it would take hours to get there.{w}\nFortaime lets out an exasperated sigh.
column6: 他指着前方远处的一座桥。{w}\n照这个速度，得花上好几个小时才能到。{w}\n福泰姆懊恼地叹了口气。

column5: Seriously!?\nHow much longer is this gonna be...?
column6: 不是吧！？\n这还要多久啊……？

column5: Oh, don't be so dramatic, Fortaime.\nWe'll be able to rest before you know it.\nEnjoy the journey. Mazeo is beautiful.
column6: 哦，别这么夸张，福泰姆。\n不知不觉我们就能休息了。\n享受这趟旅程吧。马泽奥很美。

column5: Alright...
column6: 好吧……

column5: Fortaime continues walking, defeated.{w}\nAs we inch our way forward, we start to lose hope.{w}\nHowever, it isn't long before that hope is kindled again.
column6: 福泰姆认命地继续走着。{w}\n我们一点点往前挪，开始失去希望。{w}\n然而没过多久，那份希望又重新燃起。

column5: Hey, Damek!
column6: 嘿，达梅克！

column5: A voice shouts from high up, and we turn to look.{w}\nThere's a man at the top of one of the ships, acting as a lookout.{w}\nAfter seeing Damek, he quickly makes his way down to all of us.
column6: 高处传来一声呼喊，我们转头看去。{w}\n有个人在其中一艘船的顶端，充当瞭望员。{w}\n看到达梅克后，他迅速朝我们这边下来。

column5: He slides down a ladder, quickly making his way to the surface.{w}\nStanding on the edge of the ship, he grips the railing tight.
column6: 他顺着梯子滑下，很快来到地面。{w}\n站在船沿上，他紧紧抓着栏杆。

column5: Where have you been...?\nIt feels like I haven't seen you in ages!
column6: 你去哪儿了……？\n感觉好久没见到你了！

column5: He jumps over the edge of the ship, landing on the ground with style.{w}\nI can tell he's a pirate, and he must be another ally. That was good.{w}\nIn the upcoming battle, we'd need as many allies as possible.
column6: 他从船沿跃下，潇洒地落在地上。{w}\n我看得出他是个海盗，而且一定是又一个盟友。这很好。{w}\n在即将到来的战斗中，我们需要尽可能多的盟友。

column5: Grayson! It's good to see you again.\nDon't worry, it's nothing personal. I'm just busy.\nWe've been cooking up something really special.
column6: 格雷森！很高兴又见到你。\n别担心，不是针对你。我只是太忙了。\n我们一直在筹划一件非常特别的事。

column5: Special, huh...?\nWell, that's all you had to say.\nYou know I've got your back in {i}everything{/i}.
column6: 特别，是吧……？\n嗯，你早这么说不就行了。\n你知道{i}任何事{/i}我都挺你。

column5: Damek steps closer, and whispers in Grayson's ear.{w}\nNo doubt he's confiding in Grayson about our recent choice.
column6: 达梅克走近了些，在格雷森耳边低语。{w}\n他一定是在向格雷森吐露我们最近的选择。

column5: Oh, an alliance...?\nBeautiful! We'll be working together more, then.\nAnd I must say, you made a fine decision, Damek.
column6: 哦，结盟……？\n太好了！那我们会更多地合作了。\n不得不说，你做了个明智的决定，达梅克。

column5: He smiles, and makes an interesting signal with his arms.{w}\nA few moments later, a bunch of people in our way quickly move.
column6: 他笑了笑，用手臂做了个有趣的手势。{w}\n片刻之后，挡在我们路上的一群人迅速让开了。

column5: Gotta get back to the church, I'm guessing?\nSorry about my crew. They're good at getting in the way.\nIn fact, I'm not sure what else they're good for these days.
column6: 我猜，你们得回教堂去？\n抱歉我的船员挡了路。他们很擅长挡道。\n其实，我不确定他们如今还有什么别的用处。

column5: Between every few words, he glances behind Damek.{w}\nHis eyes shift between Valessa, Fortaime, and myself.
column6: 每说几句，他就朝达梅克身后瞥一眼。{w}\n他的目光在瓦莱莎、福泰姆和我之间游移。

column5: Can I help you with something...?
column6: 有什么我能帮你的吗……？

column5: Oh, sorry, not at all!\nYou just looked familiar, that's all.\nLike some pirates Nada used to work with.
column6: 哦，抱歉，没有没有！\n只是你看起来有点眼熟，仅此而已。\n像纳达以前合作过的几个海盗。

column5: Familiar...? \nGryz said the same thing, actually.\nJust one of those faces, I guess.
column6: 眼熟……？\n其实格瑞兹也说过同样的话。\n我想只是那种大众脸吧。

column5: Not just {i}any{/i} faces, mind you.\nI was taken aback because you looked like legends.\nA few infamous pirates from back in the day, you know?
column6: 可不是{i}随便{/i}什么脸，你听好了。\n我吃了一惊，是因为你们长得像传说中的人物。\n从前几个臭名昭著的海盗，你知道吗？

column5: Pirates...?\nNo relation, I assure you.
column6: 海盗……？\n我向你保证，毫无关系。

column5: She laughs, and Grayson nods.
column6: 她笑了，格雷森点点头。

column5: Yeah, just a small world.
column6: 是啊，世界真小。

column5: It seems like he's unsure if that's an insult or not.{w}\nAnd for that matter, so does Valessa. Grayson lets it slide.{w}\nA few moments later, he climbs up a netting on the side of the ship.
column6: 他似乎不确定那算不算侮辱。{w}\n同样，瓦莱莎也不确定。格雷森没追究。{w}\n片刻之后，他攀上船舷的网缆。

column5: It isn't much longer until he's back to the top of the mast, looking out.{w}\nHe shouts to his crew, and they move aside, leaving an open trail for us.{w}\nWere all of these pirates his crew? He must be a man of great influence.
column6: 没过多久，他就回到了桅杆顶端，向外眺望。{w}\n他朝船员们喊了几句，他们让到一边，给我们让出一条路。{w}\n这些海盗都是他的船员吗？他一定是个极有影响力的人物。

column5: It's always good to have friends in high places.
column6: 在高处有朋友总是好的。

column5: There's still people wandering the shipyard, but not as many as before.{w}\nIn fact, we'd be able to continue forward without any issue at all.
column6: 船坞里还有人四处走动，但没之前那么多了。{w}\n事实上，我们完全可以毫无阻碍地继续前进了。

column5: That was Grayson, we go way back.\nHe's a great ally, and he'll have our back no matter what.\nI doubt he cares whether we sided with Alex or Nada.
column6: 那是格雷森，我们是老交情了。\n他是个绝佳的盟友，无论如何都会支持我们。\n我怀疑他根本不在乎我们站的是亚历克斯还是纳达。

column5: That was good. His crew seemed massive.{w}\nThe ship as well, was in pristine condition.
column6: 这很不错。他的船员看起来阵容庞大。{w}\n那艘船也保养得崭新如初。

column5: Well then, on we go...?
column6: 那么，我们继续走吧……？

column5: As he talks, he motions to the bridge once more.{w}\nWe give each other some space, happy to be moving freely again.{w}\nI guess we could resume our journey without any struggles.
column6: 他一边说着，一边再次指向那座桥。{w}\n我们彼此拉开些距离，很高兴又能自由行动了。{w}\n看来我们可以毫无阻碍地继续旅程了。

column5: After what feels like ages, we reach the end of the bridge.{w}\nWe all stop and catch our breath, and let our legs relax.{w}\nDamek wipes some sweat from his brow, laughing.
column6: 仿佛过了很久很久，我们终于走到了桥的另一端。{w}\n我们都停下来喘口气，让双腿放松一下。{w}\n达梅克笑着擦了擦额头的汗。

column5: A bit of a workout, isn't it?\nHopefully, the trek was worth it.\nSo — what do you think of our home?
column6: 算是锻炼了一下，对吧？\n希望这趟跋涉是值得的。\n那么——你觉得我们的家怎么样？

column5: He stands proud, staring at the nearby church.{w}\nAfter getting our bearings back, we look on in awe.
column6: 他自豪地站着，凝视着近旁的教堂。{w}\n等我们缓过神来，我们敬畏地望了过去。

column5: Whoa, this place is crazy!\nI've never seen anything like it before.
column6: 哇，这地方太疯狂了！\n我以前从没见过这样的东西。

column5: Yeah, it sure stands out, doesn't it?\nDon't worry — that works to our advantage.\nWhen hiding, I find the most obvious spot is the best.
column6: 是啊，它确实很显眼，对吧？\n别担心——这对我们有利。\n要藏身的时候，我发现最显眼的地方反而最好。

column5: I guess they'd never expect their own church.\nBut here's a question: why are there only two statues?\nIt's The Triumvirate, right? Shouldn't there be three?
column6: 我猜他们绝不会想到自己的教堂。\n但有个问题：为什么只有两尊雕像？\n那是三人执政团，对吧？不应该有三尊吗？

column5: I don't know, actually.\nIt's a bit odd, when you think about it.\nMaybe they just didn't have enough space?
column6: 其实我也不知道。\n仔细想想，这确实有点奇怪。\n也许只是空间不够吧？

column5: He laughs, awkwardly shuffling in place.{w}\nPerhaps he found his ignorance embarrassing.
column6: 他笑了，尴尬地挪了挪脚。{w}\n也许他觉得自己的无知很丢脸。

column5: I trust you're ready for the grand tour?
column6: 我想你准备好参观了吧？

column5: I nod, looking over to Valessa and Fortaime.{w}\nIt seemed our long journey was over. We were here.{w}\nThis was our new home, whether we liked it or not.
column6: 我点点头，看向瓦莱莎和福泰姆。{w}\n看来我们漫长的旅途结束了。我们到了。{w}\n无论我们喜不喜欢，这就是我们的新家。

column5: Yeah, I can't wait to see!
column6: 是啊，我等不及想看了！

column5: I'm game. Let's do this.
column6: 我奉陪。走吧。

column5: They both smile, ready to get things moving.{w}\nDamek takes a few steps up the stairs, and waves me over.
column6: 他们都笑了，准备动身。{w}\n达梅克走上几级台阶，挥手叫我过去。

column5: After you, of course.\nIt would be rude to do this any other way.\nAn esteemed guest of ours should always be first.
column6: 当然，您先请。\n换成别的方式就太失礼了。\n我们尊敬的客人理应走在最前。

column5: I nod, and get ready to enter the church.{w}\nUlric, Pro, Valessa and Fortaime wait for my move.{w}\nIt seems almost everybody respected Damek's authority.
column6: 我点点头，准备走进教堂。{w}\n乌尔里克、普洛、瓦莱莎和福泰姆都等着我的动作。{w}\n似乎几乎所有人都尊重达梅克的权威。

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: Not really, to be honest.\nYou've already seen pretty much all it has to offer.\nIt's constantly busy, and it never really stops.
column6: 老实说，没什么特别的。\n能看的你基本都看过了。\n它总是那么忙碌，从不停歇。

column5: I can't even imagine living close to the docks.\nThey work overnight, so it'd be too loud to sleep.\nThe best places are either Gryz's area, or our HQ.
column6: 我根本无法想象住在码头附近。\n他们通宵干活，吵得根本睡不着。\n最好的地方要么是格瑞兹那片，要么就是我们的总部。

column5: So maybe we can talk more about that once you see it.\nIt's so silent underground, you can hear almost everything.\nMakes it pretty easy to sleep. If you get the time, that is.
column6: 所以等你看到之后，我们也许可以再细聊。\n地下那么安静，简直什么都能听见。\n很容易入睡。前提是你有时间睡的话。

column5: She's pretty cool. Seems to be pretty by-the-book.\nI mean, I don't see her breaking any laws, or anything.\nI don't roll like that. Obviously, I live in a moral gray area.
column6: 她挺酷的。看起来是个循规蹈矩的人。\n我是说，我可看不出她会违法乱纪什么的。\n我可不那样。显然，我活在道德的灰色地带。

column5: That's not to say that she's uninteresting, though.\nI just don't see myself getting too close to her.\nIt's better for me to stick to like-minded people.
column6: 不过这不是说她无趣。\n我只是觉得自己不会跟她太亲近。\n我还是跟志同道合的人来往比较好。

column5: Who knows, maybe she'll prove me wrong.\nWar has its way of compromising almost everybody.\nI was born into this life, but I'm sure others can adapt to it.
column6: 谁知道呢，也许她会证明我错了。\n战争总有办法让几乎所有人都做出妥协。\n我生来就活在这种生活里，但我相信别人也能适应。

column5: Now he's a guy I could see myself getting along with.\nCan't wait to spend some more time with him in our HQ.\nHe speaks his mind, he's energetic, and he's careless.
column6: 他倒是那种我觉得能合得来的人。\n等不及在总部跟他多相处一阵了。\n他有什么说什么，精力充沛，而且大大咧咧。

column5: Wait, am I talking about him, or myself right now?\nYeah, you get the idea. We're like peas in a pod.\nI'm sure we'll have no shortage of good times.
column6: 等等，我现在说的是他，还是我自己？\n是啊，你懂我的意思。我们简直一个模子里刻出来的。\n我相信我们会有大把开心时光。

column5: Whoa, you sure like putting me on the spot.\nI think you're cool? I mean, from what I've seen.\nAt first, I didn't really have a clue. But it's better now.
column6: 哇，你可真喜欢当着人面问我。\n我觉得你挺酷的？我是说，就我目前所见。\n一开始我其实没什么概念。但现在好多了。

column5: You've had to make some tough decisions, [firstname].\nThat's one way to gain my respect. Push through adversity.\nI still want a one-on-one interview with you in the future, though.
column6: 你不得不做些艰难的决定，[firstname]。\n这是赢得我尊重的一种方式。迎难而上。\n不过以后我还是想跟你单独做个访谈。

column5: You've had to make some tough decisions, [firstname].\nThat's one way to gain my respect. Push through adversity.\nI still want a one-on-one interview with you in the future, though.
column6: 你不得不做些艰难的决定，[firstname]。\n这是赢得我尊重的一种方式。迎难而上。\n不过以后我还是想跟你单独做个访谈。

column5: It seems like you're starting to become quite important.\nI'd hate myself if I missed the opportunity to probe your mind.\nThat's something we can talk about later on, though. We're busy.
column6: 看来你开始变得相当重要了。\n要是错过了探究你内心的机会，我会恨自己的。\n不过那可以以后再谈。我们现在很忙。

column5: Well, pretty much every day.\nExcept for the last couple of weeks, since I was in Valinorth.\nIt's not too bad once you get used to it. I absolutely adore walking.
column6: 嗯，基本上每天吧。\n除了最近这几周，因为我在瓦利诺斯。\n习惯了之后其实还不错。我特别爱走路。

column5: It just takes some getting used to, that's all.\nSometimes, when I have it in me, I can even sprint!\nRunning to the market from our HQ is pretty intense.
column6: 只是需要适应一下，仅此而已。\n有时候，要是我有那个劲头，我甚至能冲刺！\n从总部跑到集市还挺累人的。

column5: Nobody is interested in doing it with me, though.\nI need a workout partner to keep things interesting, you know?\nEverybody else defines \"working out\" as sparring in the barracks.
column6: 不过没人有兴趣跟我一起。\n我需要个锻炼搭档，才不至于无聊，你懂吗？\n别人把“锻炼”定义为在营房里对练。

column5: So, Ulric...
column6: 那么，乌尔里克……

column5: Yeah?
column6: 嗯？

column5: I saw you and [firstname] in that tavern.\nYou two were getting {i}awfully{/i} close.
column6: 我看到你和[firstname]在那个酒馆里。\n你们俩走得{i}可真是{/i}近啊。

column5: I saw you and [firstname] in that tavern.\nYou two were getting {i}awfully{/i} close.
column6: 我看到你和[firstname]在那个酒馆里。\n你们俩走得{i}可真是{/i}近啊。

column5: Your point is...?
column6: 你想说什么……？

column5: You know we're kinda dating, right?\nWe had our first date in the town square.
column6: 你知道我们算是交往中吧？\n我们的第一次约会就在城镇广场。

column5: Oh, that's what that was?
column6: 哦，原来那是约会啊？

column5: Yeah, and it was pretty awesome!\nMostly thanks to you though, and that apple.
column6: 是啊，而且超棒的！\n不过主要还是多亏了你，还有那个苹果。

column5: I was hoping you'd share it together.\nMaybe I was playing matchmaker all along.
column6: 我是希望你们能一起分享。\n也许我一直都在当红娘。

column5: Yeah, right! Nobody is {i}that{/i} smart.
column6: 得了吧！没人{i}那么{/i}聪明。

column5: You're not giving me enough credit, little one.\nAnyway — you don't mind that we're...?
column6: 你太低估我了，小家伙。\n总之——你不介意我们……？

column5: Oh, of course not! The more the merrier!\n[firstname] has a lot of love to go around.
column6: 哦，当然不介意！人越多越热闹！\n[firstname]的爱多得可以分给很多人。

column5: Oh, of course not! The more the merrier!\n[firstname] has a lot of love to go around.
column6: 哦，当然不介意！人越多越热闹！\n[firstname]的爱多得可以分给很多人。

column5: Yeah. More than I thought, actually.\nI'm sure you and I will be getting closer now, too.
column6: 是啊。其实比我以为的还多。\n我相信你和我现在也会更亲近了。

column5: No objections here!
column6: 我没意见！

column5: I was just gonna say, that's pretty cool!
column6: 我正想说，那挺酷的！

column5: Really?
column6: 真的？

column5: He never had time for that stuff back in Valinorth, so yeah.\nIt's good to see things changing now that we're on the road.\nI didn't know this would happen. I guess I missed my chance.
column6: 在瓦利诺斯的时候他从来抽不出时间搞这些，所以是啊。\n上路之后能看到事情有变化，真好。\n我没想到会这样。看来我错过机会了。

column5: She never had time for that stuff back in Valinorth, so yeah.\nIt's good to see things changing now that we're on the road.\nI didn't know this would happen. I guess I missed my chance.
column6: 在瓦利诺斯的时候她从来抽不出时间搞这些，所以是啊。\n上路之后能看到事情有变化，真好。\n我没想到会这样。看来我错过机会了。

column5: Wait, are you jealous...?
column6: 等等，你在吃醋……？

column5: No! Not at all!
column6: 没有！完全没有！

column5: Sure.
column6: 当然。

column5: Ulric, I'm serious!
column6: 乌尔里克，我是认真的！

column5: You know, you're still free to see him if you want to.\nOr is the culture in Valinorth different than everywhere else?
column6: 你知道的，如果你想，你随时可以去找他。\n还是说瓦利诺斯的文化跟别处不一样？

column5: You know, you're still free to see her if you want to.\nOr is the culture in Valinorth different than everywhere else?
column6: 你知道的，如果你想，你随时可以去找她。\n还是说瓦利诺斯的文化跟别处不一样？

column5: What do you mean..?
column6: 你什么意思……？

column5: It's normal for people to have more than one partner.\nI thought the same went for Valinorth, actually.
column6: 一个人有多个伴侣是很正常的。\n其实我还以为瓦利诺斯也是这样。

column5: Oh, it does...!\nSorry, I must've misunderstood.
column6: 哦，是的……！\n抱歉，我一定误会了。

column5: You're just dodging the issue, aren't you?\nFortaime, it's okay to admit if you like [firstname].
column6: 你只是在回避问题，对吧？\n福泰姆，承认你喜欢[firstname]也没关系。

column5: You're just dodging the issue, aren't you?\nFortaime, it's okay to admit if you like [firstname].
column6: 你只是在回避问题，对吧？\n福泰姆，承认你喜欢[firstname]也没关系。

column5: Never!
column6: 绝不！

column5: This party banter is due to your relationship with Ulric.
column6: 这段队伍闲聊是因为你与乌尔里克的关系。

column5: That's the bridge we used to come here.{w}\nIt was structurally sound, but didn't feel like it.{w}\nPart of me was scared it'd fall apart from under us.
column6: 那就是我们来时走过的桥。{w}\n结构上很稳固，但感觉不像。{w}\n我有点害怕它会从我们脚下塌掉。

column5: Damek showed no signs of worry, however.{w}\nThat put me at ease, since he was a local.{w}\nIf he was scared, I knew I'd be, as well.
column6: 不过达梅克毫无担忧的迹象。{w}\n这让我安心了，因为他是本地人。{w}\n如果他害怕，我知道我也会怕。

column5: It's a statue of a cloaked figure.{w}\nBut we're not sure {i}who{/i} it's supposed to be.{w}\nThere's only two of them. It can't be The Triumvirate.
column6: 那是一尊披斗篷人物的雕像。{w}\n但我们不确定它{i}该是{/i}谁。{w}\n只有两尊。不可能是三人执政团。

column5: If it were, then there'd be three statues.{w}\nBut where would the third statue go anyway?{w}\nMaybe it was just a space limitation thing.
column6: 如果是的话，就该有三尊雕像。{w}\n但第三尊雕像又能放哪儿呢？{w}\n也许只是空间受限吧。

column5: Either way, they look mysterious and brooding.{w}\nIt makes the entire church give off an eerie vibe.{w}\nThe architectural style wasn't helping it, either.
column6: 不管怎样，它们看起来神秘而阴沉。{w}\n让整座教堂散发出一种诡异的氛围。{w}\n建筑风格也帮不上忙。

column5: The church looks so out of place.{w}\nI've never seen anything like it before.{w}\nIt doesn't look Mazean, that's for sure.
column6: 这座教堂看起来格格不入。{w}\n我以前从没见过这样的东西。{w}\n它肯定不像马泽奥的风格。

column5: It looks creepy...
column6: 看起来好瘆人……

column5: It's modelled after Balteus.\nThat's what things look like over there.
column6: 它是仿照巴尔泰乌斯建的。\n那边的东西就长这样。

column5: And that's where we're going next.\nJust great. Now I'm even more afraid.\nWho makes stuff like this anyway...?
column6: 而我们下一站就是去那儿。\n好极了。现在我更害怕了。\n到底是谁造出这种东西的……？

column5: Your guess is as good as mine.\nIt doesn't fit in with any part of Alestia.\nBalteus is really distinct. It's kind of cool.
column6: 我和你一样不知道。\n它跟阿莱斯提亚的任何地方都不搭。\n巴尔泰乌斯真的很独特。挺酷的。

column5: I'll take your word for it...
column6: 我就信你一回……

column5: As soon as we enter, Damek walks down the center aisle.{w}\nHe trails a finger along the pews as he does, gathering up dust.
column6: 我们一进去，达梅克就沿着中央过道往前走。{w}\n他一边走一边用手指划过长椅，沾起灰尘。

column5: Not much time for Triumvirate worship these days.
column6: 如今没什么时间祭拜三人执政团了。

column5: He makes his way to the spirit idol at the back of the church.{w}\nClapping his hands together, he frees himself of the dust.
column6: 他走向教堂后方的灵界灵像。{w}\n他双手一拍，抖掉手上的灰尘。

column5: This is the spirit idol of Mazeo.\nOr so we thought, until recently.
column6: 这是马泽奥的灵界灵像。\n至少我们以前是这么以为的，直到最近。

column5: It remains dust free, unlike the rest of the church.{w}\nHe places a hand on the altar, looking up at the idol.
column6: 它一尘不染，不像教堂的其他地方。{w}\n他把一只手放在祭坛上，抬头望着灵像。

column5: We assumed it was dim, and dying.\nYou know, like the idol back in Valinorth.\nBut that's not the case at all. We were shocked.
column6: 我们以为它黯淡无光，正在消亡。\n你知道的，就像瓦利诺斯的那尊灵像。\n但根本不是那么回事。我们都惊呆了。

column5: The reason it's dim, is because it's receiving power.\nHowever, the source of power is deep underground.\nThat's what The Triumvirate has been digging for.
column6: 它之所以黯淡，是因为它正在接收能量。\n然而，能量的源头在地下深处。\n那正是三人执政团一直在挖掘的东西。

column5: The entire reason for their occupation...\nAnd now it's in the hands of The Rebellion.\nFirst their sword, now the idol they sought.
column6: 他们占领此地的全部理由……\n而现在它落到了反抗军手里。\n先是他们的剑，现在是他们苦苦寻找的灵像。

column5: He turns back to face us, a wide smile on his face.
column6: 他转过身面向我们，脸上挂着灿烂的笑容。

column5: It would seem the tables are turning.\nFeel free to rest for a few minutes.\nThere's still a bit of a walk ahead.
column6: 看来局势正在逆转。\n你们随意休息几分钟吧。\n前面还有一段路要走。

column5: Seriously!? More walking...?\nWhen are we gonna get to rest?
column6: 不是吧！？还要走……？\n我们什么时候才能休息啊？

column5: Trust me, you'll get plenty of time to rest.\nJust take a breather before we continue.
column6: 相信我，你会有一大把时间休息的。\n继续出发前先喘口气吧。

column5: He points to the pews before walking over to a door in the back corner.
column6: 他指了指长椅，然后走向后角落的一扇门。

column5: This door will lead us to the tunnels, [firstname].\nIt's the final stretch, I can promise you that.\nWhenever you're ready, let's head on down.
column6: 这扇门会带我们去隧道，[firstname]。\n这是最后一段路了，我可以向你保证。\n你准备好就下去吧。

column5: This door will lead us to the tunnels, [firstname].\nIt's the final stretch, I can promise you that.\nWhenever you're ready, let's head on down.
column6: 这扇门会带我们去隧道，[firstname]。\n这是最后一段路了，我可以向你保证。\n你准备好就下去吧。

column5: He presses his back against the wall, and crosses his arms.{w}\nEveryone seems glad that he was offering us a brief reprieve.{w}\nI'd take a few moments to collect myself before we head down.
column6: 他把背靠在墙上，双臂交叉。{w}\n他似乎给了我们短暂的喘息机会，大家都很高兴。{w}\n下去之前，我要花点时间整理一下自己。

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: It's crazy! I don't know what to think.\nJust when I'm comfortable, something new is thrown at us.\nThe markets, the residential districts, {i}and{/i} the docks?
column6: 太疯狂了！我都不知道该作何感想。\n我刚觉得自在一点，就又冒出些新东西。\n集市、住宅区，{i}还有{/i}码头？

column5: Valinorth is pretty much the same no matter where you are.\nTo see things so different? That's a real shocker for me.\nI'm not sure what my favorite part has been, so far.
column6: 瓦利诺斯不管在哪儿都差不多一个样。\n看到这么不同的景象？对我来说真是大开眼界。\n到目前为止，我还不确定自己最喜欢哪一部分。

column5: If I had to choose though, I'd say the residential district.\nBeing able to live free from the noise, and free of work?\nThat's like a dream come true. Everywhere is so {i}noisy{/i}.
column6: 不过如果非要选，我会选住宅区。\n能住在没有噪音、不用干活的地方？\n简直像梦想成真。到处都是那么{i}吵{/i}。

column5: I assume you get used to the noise, but it's still {i}there{/i}.\nYou know what I mean, right? You just learn to ignore it.\nI'd rather not have to do that, it'd make things way easier.
column6: 我想人是会习惯噪音的，但它依然{i}在那儿{/i}。\n你懂我的意思吧？你只是学会忽略它。\n我倒希望不用这样，那样会轻松得多。

column5: He's so cool! I love being around him.\nI want to learn to be more like him, if I'm honest.\nEverybody respects him, and follows his directions.
column6: 他好酷！我喜欢待在他身边。\n老实说，我想学着变得更像他。\n大家都尊敬他，听从他的指示。

column5: He's going to make a fine leader after this is over.\nI actually doubted The Rebellion, but he convinced me.\nThis cause is in perfect hands. We're {i}going{/i} to do this.
column6: 等这一切结束后，他会成为一位出色的领袖。\n我其实曾怀疑过反抗军，但他说服了我。\n这个事业交到了最合适的人手里。我们{i}一定{/i}能做到。

column5: I didn't trust him at first, but he's growing on me.\nI know he does a lot of shady things, but only out of necessity.\nI have no doubt in my mind that after the war is over, he'll change.
column6: 我一开始不信任他，但他越来越让我喜欢。\n我知道他做很多见不得光的事，但都是出于不得已。\n我毫不怀疑，战争结束后他会改变的。

column5: Ulric is probably my favorite person, so far.\nI mean — he gave me free money earlier. Free!\nIt's all thanks to him that I got to taste a Mazean apple.
column6: 到目前为止，乌尔里克大概是我最喜欢的人。\n我是说——他刚才还白给了我钱。白给的！\n全靠他，我才尝到了马泽奥的苹果。

column5: That's the {i}one{/i} thing I was looking forward to.\nHe's been nothing but friendly since we met him.\nSure he seems strong, but he's really gentle.
column6: 那正是我{i}唯一{/i}期待的东西。\n从认识他以来，他一直都很友善。\n他看上去确实很强，但其实很温柔。

column5: Who would've thought that a guy like him has a soft side?\nEither way, yeah, Ulric has been great. He's teaching me a lot.\nMaybe one day I might even learn how to use a greatsword like him!
column6: 谁能想到他这样的人还有温柔的一面？\n不管怎样，是啊，乌尔里克一直很棒。他教了我很多。\n也许有一天我甚至能学会像他那样用巨剑！

column5: I feel great. There's not much to say.\nWe have everything we need in order to win.\nI can't wait to see our new HQ. Our new home.
column6: 我感觉好极了。没什么好说的。\n我们拥有了取胜所需的一切。\n我迫不及待想看到我们的新总部。我们的新家。

column5: The sun shines with intensity, illuminating the interior of the church.{w}\nI can see every bit of dust lining the floor and the pews.{w}\nI guess they spent more time dusting underground.
column6: 阳光强烈地照射进来，照亮了教堂内部。{w}\n我能看清地板和长椅上每一粒灰尘。{w}\n我猜他们把更多时间花在了打扫地下。

column5: Hey, Fortaime?
column6: 嘿，福泰姆？

column5: Yeah?
column6: 嗯？

column5: I saw you and [firstname] run off into an alley earlier.\nWhat were you two doing back there, exactly?
column6: 我看到你刚才和[firstname]跑进一条小巷。\n你们俩到底在后面做什么？

column5: I saw you and [firstname] run off into an alley earlier.\nWhat were you two doing back there, exactly?
column6: 我看到你刚才和[firstname]跑进一条小巷。\n你们俩到底在后面做什么？

column5: Oh, we were on a {i}date{/i}!
column6: 哦，我们在{i}约会{/i}！

column5: What!? Seriously...?
column6: 什么！？真的假的……？

column5: Whoa, don't act so surprised — you might hurt me.
column6: 哇，别表现得这么惊讶——你会伤到我的。
